Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for an Equivalence-Test SMD

Source: R/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity.Rd

Quantifies how much misspecification of the population standardized mean difference distorts an AIPE-based sample size plan for the two-one-sided-tests (TOST) confidence interval on the standardized mean difference. On each replication the function simulates two normal groups of size n per group with population standardized mean difference true_smd, computes the sample standardized mean difference and the interval equivalence_smd reports for it, and summarizes the realized widths, the proportion of replications in which the interval falls entirely inside the equivalence bounds (equivalent), and the proportions that miss true_smd.

Usage

ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity(
  true_smd = 0,
  supposed_smd = NULL,
  width,
  smd_lower = NULL,
  smd_upper = NULL,
  specified_n_per_group = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_smd

Population standardized mean difference (the data generating value), a single finite number. Defaults to 0 (perfect equivalence).

supposed_smd

The supposed population SMD, the planning value passed to ss_aipe_equivalence_smd (not an estimate computed from data), a single finite number; supply this or specified_n_per_group but not both.

width

Desired full width of the two-sided CI on the SMD.

smd_lower, smd_upper

Equivalence bounds on the SMD, as positive magnitudes with the same meaning as in equivalence_smd: the region is \((-\delta_L, +\delta_U)\), with smd_lower as \(\delta_L\) and smd_upper as \(\delta_U\). smd_upper is required; smd_lower defaults to smd_upper (a symmetric region). The simulator records whether the realized CI falls entirely inside the region.

specified_n_per_group

Per-group sample size to evaluate, a whole number of at least 2.

conf_level

Confidence level of the interval (default 0.95); the two one-sided tests it decides are at level (1 - conf_level) / 2.

assurance

Optional assurance probability, passed to ss_aipe_equivalence_smd when the sample size is planned from supposed_smd.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications.

print_iter

Logical.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the sample standardized mean difference, the two confidence limits, the interval width, whether the interval fell inside the equivalence region, and two indicators of whether the interval missed true_smd below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with rows for mean / median / SD of the realized SMD and CI width, the proportion of intervals at or below width, tail-specific and overall non-coverage of true_smd, the proportion of intervals classified as equivalent (CI fully inside the bounds), and the input echoes, including assurance (present only when an assurance was supplied).

Details

The interval simulated. The interval is the one equivalence_smd reports and ss_aipe_equivalence_smd plans for, $$\hat d \pm t_{1 - \alpha,\, 2n - 2} \sqrt{(8 + \hat d^{\,2}) / (4n)},$$ a large-sample standard error of \(\hat d\) with a Student t critical value, at confidence level conf_level, so that \(\alpha\) is (1 - conf_level) / 2: the default 0.95 is the interval of the two one-sided tests at \(\alpha = .025\), and conf_level = 0.90 is the interval of the tests at .05. A sample size from supposed_smd is planned by ss_aipe_equivalence_smd(alpha_level = (1 - conf_level) / 2), so the plan, the analysis, and the simulation describe one interval at one level: a simulated sample with standardized mean difference \(\hat d\) gives the limits equivalence_smd(smd = d, n_1 = n, n_2 = n, alpha_level = (1 - conf_level) / 2) reports. When true_smd equals supposed_smd, pct_ci_less_width estimates the probability that the interval at the planned size is no wider than width, which the planner computes and reports as assurance_attained when assurance is given; the simulation attribute (below) gives the Monte Carlo limits of the estimate.

The interval is a large-sample approximation, so its coverage of true_smd (the pct_ci_miss_low, pct_ci_miss_high, and total_type_I_error rows) can differ from 1 - conf_level, most in small samples; the noncentral t interval of ci_smd, which ss_aipe_smd_sensitivity simulates, has exact coverage for the normal model.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11, 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Examples

# Reduced Monte Carlo sweep (small G) for a fast, illustrative run.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity(
  true_smd      = 0.0,
  supposed_smd  = 0.0,
  width         = 0.30,
  smd_upper     = 0.20,
  G = 50, print_iter = FALSE
)
